channel_identity.positioning: Impactful historical facts, documented and verifiable. Not mysteries, not the unexplained, not UFOs, not cosmic threats.

growth_model.expansion_rule: If a short exceeds 5x channel short median views within 48h, enqueue a 8-15 min long-form sibling within 7 days.

criteria: Measurable scale (deaths, km, levels, magnitude, years, soldiers)
Proper name or secret place people can search
Impossible premise or twist usable in first 2 seconds
Not saturated on this channel (avoid 3rd Tunguska / same quake retread)
reject_if: Abstract science with no historical event
Generic list without a single anchor event
Duplicate of an existing channel title angle
Modern explosion/quake/eruption as the ONLY angle of a YouTube Short (0 of 4 took off, sep-2026); ok on Facebook or with a mechanism/person angle
Mystery framing ('mystery invaders', 'unexplained', 'curse') - 0 of 3 took off, sep-2026

shorts_rules.sweet_spot_note: Medido sobre 223 videos: entre 45 y 90s el percentil es plano (0.42-0.53), o sea la duracion no discrimina. Los de 91-180s rinden igual y generan 13x mas watch time. Se sube el objetivo a 80s para contar una historia con final, que es lo que genera motivo para volver.
shorts_rules.cadence_note: 1 short por dia. El canal anterior publicaba 2+/dia y sus mejores meses fueron justamente los de mas volumen (marzo: 66 subidas, mediana 80 views; abril: 58, mediana 113). Lo que si lo hundio fue el 20% de casi-duplicados y la caida de retencion a 39.4% en julio. La cadencia diaria solo es sostenible con: cero duplicados, el bloque de QA en verde, y series con continuidad.

long_form_rules.evidence_2026_11: 12 meses: long-form = 683 vistas / 16,4 h (Shorts 54.106 vistas, no cuentan para YPP). 0 vistas de BROWSE. Retencion: se va el 41-55% en los primeros 30 s y hay un segundo derrumbe entre el 20% y el 30% del video. Rendimiento relativo vs videos similares 0,05-0,50. Los temas SI tienen demanda (Dyatlov mediana 195k, Sea Peoples: canal de 13,9k subs con 341k vistas); fallan empaque y apertura.
long_form_rules.topic_gate: Solo temas con demanda medida en busqueda de YouTube (videos 4-20 min desde 2024): mediana >10k vistas o al menos un canal <50k subs con >20k vistas. Herramienta: long_form_research.py demand "<tema>" (ver playbook 6d).
first_30_seconds: Primera frase = escena concreta con fecha, lugar y escala (persona, lugar u objeto real); nada de 'This is the story of' ni prosa abstracta.
La consecuencia o el contraste antes de los 30 s (cuantos murieron, que se perdio, por que solo una vez): lo que esta en juego, no la explicacion completa.
Repetir la pregunta del titulo hacia los 35 s y prometer el pago; se puede adelantar la tesis en una frase y explicarla despues (outlier Buran).
Una cifra concreta en los primeros 40 s; nada de contexto tecnico ni de fondo antes de que la tension este planteada (Skylab y Damascus se hundieron entre el 10 % y el 30 %).
structure: Cold open 45-75 s: escena + pregunta + promesa (sin titulo animado largo)
Narracion por misterio/investigacion, no cronologica: cada capitulo abre con una pregunta y cierra con un gancho al siguiente
Una prueba o giro nuevo cada 60-90 s; interrupcion de patron al 25% y al 50% (cambio visual fuerte, dato inesperado)
Evidencia / teorias rivales con veredicto honesto
Pago de la pregunta del cold open en los ultimos 2 minutos, luego cierre corto + video siguiente en pantalla final
packaging: Titulo: frase con tension y una cifra concreta ('The Last 77 Seconds...', '20,000 Warriors. One Morning.'); evitar 'Tema: subtitulo' y palabras genericas (disaster, history, story, explained). Max ~60 caracteres.
Miniatura: 2-4 palabras con una afirmacion o cifra fuerte ('589 DAYS', 'LANDED ITSELF. NEVER AGAIN.'), sujeto real con emocion; no repetir el titulo.
El Short hermano debe enlazar el largo (Studio > Short > 'Video relacionado'), la descripcion abre con el enlace y comentario fijado.
long_form_rules.cadence: 1 documental por semana bien hecho; no 3 en 4 dias.
long_form_rules.source: Tema con demanda medida + Short del canal que ya funciono; no inventar long-forms huerfanos
long_form_rules.evidence_hooklab_2026_11: 83 outliers del nicho (<=100k subs, >=30k vistas) vs 328: cifras en titulo 47 % vs 37 %, ':'/'|' 39 % vs 51 %. Transcripciones de 3 outliers: fecha+lugar+escala, consecuencia antes de 30 s, pregunta del titulo a los ~35 s. Muestras chicas: indicios. Detalle: ~/video-projects/hooklab/FINDINGS.md. Herramienta: python -m documentary_kit.hook_check.

hook.description: Hook brutal: la cifra extrema o el hecho imposible, dicho sin rodeos

payload.description: SEGUNDO Y TERCER HECHO CONCRETO (cifras, nombres, consecuencias). PROHIBIDO poner contexto aca: es el tramo donde se va el 35% de la audiencia. Lo prometido en el hook tiene que OCURRIR antes del s20

context.description: Recien ahora el contexto: quien decidio, que lo precedio, como fue posible. Se gano el derecho a explicarlo

consequence.description: Consecuencias documentadas: que cambio, a quien, con que evidencia

close.description: Cierra con la consecuencia que todavia importa hoy. NO cerrar insinuando un misterio abierto ni con CTA larga de suscripcion

allowed.name: Vanished / Erased
allowed.description: Something massive disappeared or was destroyed
examples: A massive city vanished without a trace.
An empire was erased from history.
They built a city for 20,000 people... underground.
They built a city larger than London... then vanished.
allowed.note: 2026-09-21: en el canal nuevo el encuadre 'vanished/mystery' murio (3 de 3 sin despegar). Usar solo con hecho documentado y cifra; nunca como misterio.

allowed.name: Impossible Question
allowed.description: A question that seems impossible or paradoxical
examples: Did a Roman legion disappear into ancient China?
What happened when the sun vanished for 18 months?
Could one corpse change the outcome of a world war?
Could one explosion flatten 80 million trees?

allowed.name: Date + Scene + Anomaly
allowed.description: Specific date anchored to a vivid, anomalous event
examples: In 536 AD, the sky went dark.
In 53 BC, Rome lost an army in the desert.
On June 8, 1783, Iceland poisoned Europe.
In 1908, Siberia exploded without a crater.

allowed.name: Extreme Scale
allowed.description: Emphasize an extreme magnitude or consequence
examples: The strongest earthquake ever recorded changed the planet.
The explosion was 1,000 times stronger than Hiroshima.
One battle destroyed an empire in a single day.
Twenty thousand people lived sixty meters underground.

allowed.name: Mechanism Question
allowed.description: HOW or WHY something worked, asked straight; the answer is measurable
examples: How did 20,000 people breathe 85 meters underground?
Why did Roman concrete get stronger underwater?

allowed.name: The Find
allowed.description: Something concrete was found, with its age or size and one twist
examples: A 5,000-year-old dress, mistaken for rags for a century.
Under the car park: a king, 500 years missing.

visual_rules.prompt_base: Cinematic documentary realism, vertical 9:16 composition, strong central subject, mobile-safe framing, dramatic contrast, atmospheric lighting, believable historical textures, clear foreground midground background depth, no text, no logos, no watermarks, no UI, no modern objects, no anachronisms.
visual_rules.negative_prompt_base: text, captions, subtitles, letters, numbers, watermark, logo, signature, UI, HUD, app interface, split screen, collage, infographic, modern city, neon lights, cars, power lines, plastic objects, modern weapons, contemporary architecture, asphalt, concrete buildings, glass windows, modern clothing, low detail, blurry, distorted faces, extra limbs, bad anatomy

narration_tone.pacing: Short sentences. Dramatic pauses. New information or visual twist every 5-8 seconds.

Who decided, and what did it cost?

items.name: How they did it
items.description: The video answers HOW or WHY something worked: the engineering, the logistics, the trick. The event is the excuse; the mechanism is the payload.
items.prompt: ANGLE = MECHANISM. The first spoken sentence is a HOW/WHY question or a concrete number about the mechanism (e.g. 'How did 20,000 people breathe 85 meters underground?'). By second 20 the viewer must have the first concrete piece of the answer: a material, a measurement, a step. Explain with numbers and named parts. No 'mystery', no speculation. Close with what the mechanism made possible.
items.thumbnail: the object or structure itself mid-process (a stone being moved, a sewer cross-section, a weapon detail); one measurable element visible; no faces
items.evidence: YouTube nicho, top 30 dias al 2026-09-21: 'How Did Romans Measure Distance?' 1.5M; 'Why WW2 Grenades Had Grooves' 486K; 'How Did Egyptians Transport 1,000-Ton Stones?' 424K; 'Cloaca Maxima' 332K; 'Why Did Medieval Archers Put Blades Behind Their Arrows?' 391K.

items.name: Discovery news
items.description: Tell it as news: WHAT was found, WHERE, WHEN, by WHOM, and the one detail that changes what we knew.
items.prompt: ANGLE = DISCOVERY. Present tense for the find, past tense for the history. First spoken sentence: the find and one number ('A 5,000-year-old dress, mistaken for rags for a century'). Name the site and the team. Say plainly what is still unknown, without 'mystery' words. Close with what it changes.
items.thumbnail: the artifact or site in situ, partially uncovered, with a scale reference (hand, tool, person from behind); no faces
items.evidence: 'Teenager Discovers Lost Ancient City?' 4.85M (230K likes); '5,000-Year-Old Dress Mistaken for Rags' 2.5M; 'Iron Sickle Around Her Neck' 373K; 'Secret City 280 Feet Underground' (Derinkuyu) 309K. Facebook propio: mejor retencion al primer cuarto (32%).

items.name: Human story
items.description: One named person or small group, one decision, one outcome.
items.prompt: ANGLE = HUMAN STORY. Open on the moment of maximum danger or the impossible fact ('He fell 18,000 feet without a parachute. He lived.'). Numbers serve the person, not the other way around. No weapon catalogues, no death tolls as the point. End with what happened to them afterwards.
items.thumbnail: the person's object or place (the parachute, the U-boat, the ice road); a lone figure from behind or in silhouette; never a centered portrait
items.evidence: 'The U-Boat That Escaped to Argentina' 5.2M con 180 s; 'He Fell 18,000 Feet Without a Parachute' 1M; 'The Ghost Army' 771K. Propio: 'Kaiten' 1,249 vistas pero 24% se quedo y 0 subs: el arma oscura atrae el swipe, la persona retiene.

items.name: Event with a number
items.description: A documented event told through ONE measurable scale in the first sentence.
items.prompt: ANGLE = SCALE EVENT. First spoken sentence carries the scale (7,000 people; 20,000 troops; 92 islets). Second and third concrete facts before second 20. Named place, named decision-maker, documented consequence. If the event is a modern explosion, quake or eruption, this angle is NOT enough on YouTube: fold in a mechanism or a person.
items.thumbnail: the place or structure at scale (walls, fleet, city) with the number legible in frame; no faces
items.evidence: Propio (2026-09-21): 'Catalhoyuk 7,000 People' 1,320 vistas / 8 subs; 'Piye 20,000 Troops' 674 / 7 subs (97% retencion); 'Nan Madol 92 Islets' 840. Desastres modernos como eje: 0 de 4 despego.

auto_rules.note: Si el Studio esta en 'auto': primero el snapshot de rendimiento (peso por angulo), despues estas palabras del tema, y si nada aplica, 'scale_event'.

first_seconds.note: Medido 2026-09-21 en los reels de Facebook de la pagina (curvas de retencion por segundo) y en YouTube (engagedViews).
rules: The FIRST spoken sentence carries a concrete number/scale OR a HOW/WHY question. Not both required, one is mandatory.
The date goes in the SECOND sentence or later. Never open with 'In 1540,' / 'On May 29, 1453,' / 'Around 1600 BC,'.
First sentence: 14 words maximum. Second sentence lands the second concrete fact before second 6.
No throat-clearing: no 'Did you know', no 'Imagine', no 'Discover', no channel name.
first_seconds.evidence: Facebook: los reels que abren con fecha ('In 1540, ...', 'On May 29, 1453, ...') retienen ~30% al primer cuarto; la mejor curva de la pagina ('They calculated six megatons. They got fifteen.') retiene 50/37/33% y no lleva fecha. YouTube: 'Piye: 20,000 Troops' 97% de retencion media.
good: They calculated six megatons. They got fifteen.
7,000 people, no streets, no doors. How did they get home?
20,000 troops crossed the desert to take Egypt.
bad: In 1540, Portuguese cannon fire toppled a 24-meter obelisk.
On May 29, 1453, the 27-foot Orban cannon thundered.
Did you know 20,000 people once lived inside a stone city?
